title: A number guessing game
description:
Read guesses from the user until they find the number.

```
Guess a number from 1 to 100.
Guess: 50
Too high
Guess: 30
Too low
Guess: 42
Got it in 3 guesses!
```
hints: `let guess: u32 = match line.trim().parse() { Ok(n) => n, Err(_) => { println!("Type a number"); continue; } };` (lesson 1.05).

`guess.cmp(&secret)` compares two numbers and gives an `Ordering`: `Ordering::Less`, `Ordering::Greater` or `Ordering::Equal`, so `match guess.cmp(&secret) { Ordering::Less => ..., Ordering::Greater => ..., Ordering::Equal => ... }` covers every case. `Ordering::Equal` is the arm that prints the result and `break`s.
requirements: The secret is fixed (`42`) or worked out from the time; no crates.
Read lines with `std::io::stdin().read_line`; text that is not a number prints `Type a number` and does not count.
stretch: Make the secret change each run with `std::time::SystemTime::now()` and the nanoseconds.
